title: The American Civil War
text: The American Civil War (1861–1865) was fought between the United States (Union) and the Confederate States of America, formed by eleven southern states that seceded over issues including slavery and states' rights. President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863, declaring enslaved people in Confederate states to be free. The war was the deadliest in American history, with approximately 620,000–750,000 soldier deaths. The Union victory preserved the United States as one nation, and the subsequent Reconstruction era attempted to reintegrate the South and establish civil rights for formerly enslaved people. The 13th Amendment to the Constitution, ratified in 1865, formally abolished slavery.
